headline: Sterling is about 1.3119 dollars on Friday morning, a little above Thursday evening's 1.3104 after the dollar softened in thin trade overnight. The pound is still pulled between a December Fed rise that markets see as all but certain, which supports the dollar, and Bank of England policymakers who say they may also need to raise rates in December if energy prices stay high.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: Traders see a quarter point Fed rise on 9 December as a near certainty, according to CME FedWatch figures cited by Reuters on 27 November, and they expect a further rise by around April after October's core PCE inflation came in at 3.3% on the year and third quarter growth was revised up. Expected Fed rises support the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound.

drivers.title: The Bank of England
drivers.text: Governor Bailey and colleagues told MPs on 25 November that they cannot ignore the inflation threat from persistently high energy prices, and markets were pricing almost an 80% chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December, according to Bloomberg figures cited by FXStreet on 26 November. Expected Bank of England rises support the pound and have limited its falls this week.

drivers.title: The dollar's range
drivers.text: The dollar index was steady at about 103.8 early on 27 November, according to Reuters, after reaching 104.53 on Monday, its highest since March of last year, and giving the gain back a day later. FXStreet noted on 26 November that GBP/USD has lost more than 3.5% since its peak near 1.3500 in early November, so the pound remains well below where it started the month.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: US crude rose above $85 a barrel (about £65) early on 27 November, its highest in over a week, according to FXStreet, after Saudi Arabia reported a strike on its Jazan refinery, following the Houthi attack claimed on 25 November. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, though high energy prices are also what keeps the Bank of England leaning towards a further rise.

lower: Fresh attacks on Gulf oil sites or shipping, or renewed falls in shares on tariff or AI worries, which tend to send investors towards the dollar and mean fewer dirhams per pound.
Any sign that Bank of England policymakers are less sure about a December rise, for example if energy prices fall back, which would take some support away from the pound.
higher: A continued risk-on mood or further falls in US Treasury yields, which would weaken the dollar and mean more dirhams per pound.
Firm UK news or Bank of England comments that keep a December rise in play, which would lift the pound.
watch: US markets reopen today for a shortened Black Friday session, so trading is likely to stay thin, and there are no major US or UK figures due. The next big events are the Fed's decision on 9 December, where markets already expect a quarter point rise, and the Bank of England's decision on 17 December; a firmer Bank of England or any sign the Fed might hold back would tend to help someone selling pounds for dirhams.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up and slipped back before the US open
feed.text: GBP/USD moved between 1.3113 and 1.3125 through the London morning, then rose from about 1.3120 at 10:55 UTC to a high of 1.3131 by 11:25 before slipping back to about 1.3121 by 11:35. EUR/USD stayed almost flat near 1.0958 over the same period, so the small rise was in the pound rather than a weaker dollar, but no report read names a cause, and with no UK or US figures due and US markets open only for a shortened Black Friday session, trading remains thin. Trading Economics notes the pound is still about 1.5% lower over the past month after touching a one year low of 1.3032 on 23 November.

feed.title: Sterling is holding steady in quiet Black Friday trade
feed.text: GBP/USD has moved in a narrow band this morning, rising from 1.3113 to a high of 1.3128 around 05:30 UTC before settling near 1.3117, with a low of 1.3111 since the last update. There are no major US or UK figures today and US markets are only open for a shortened session, so trading is thin; expected Fed rises continue to support the dollar, while bets on a Bank of England rise in December are stopping the pound from falling further. FXStreet notes that the pound is on course for its first weekly gain in four weeks.

feed.title: The dollar has softened in thin Black Friday trade
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped from about 1.3102 at 04:00 Dubai to about 1.3089 by 04:45, as the dollar firmed briefly after softer than expected Tokyo inflation figures (core 2.9% against 3.0% forecast) weakened the yen. It then rose to about 1.3127 by 07:00 Dubai and was near 1.3119 at 07:38, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share from about 1.0959 to about 1.0982, so this was broad dollar softening rather than UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single cause; FXStreet described the dollar as easing in a risk-on mood with liquidity thin on Black Friday.

feed.title: Sterling has stayed in a narrow range through the afternoon
feed.text: With US markets shut for Thanksgiving, GBP/USD has moved only between about 1.3096 and 1.3120 since the last update, rising from near 1.3097 at 17:15 Dubai to its high around 18:00 and then drifting back to about 1.3104, almost exactly where it stood four hours ago. No report read names a cause for the small rise, and the picture is unchanged: a December Fed rise is still seen as all but certain, which supports the dollar, while the chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December supports the pound.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady in quiet holiday trade
feed.text: With US markets shut for Thanksgiving, GBP/USD has moved only between 1.3092 and 1.3118 since this morning's update and stands near 1.3105, almost exactly where it was. A dip to the low of the range between about 11:15 and 11:45 UTC was not explained by any report found, and it recovered within the hour. ING said it expects very quiet markets, with a December Fed rise still seen as all but certain, which keeps the dollar supported.

feed.title: The Bank of England has eased bank capital rules
feed.text: The Bank of England's Financial Stability Report on 26 November lowered capital requirements for the largest UK banks by the equivalent of about half a percentage point, kept the countercyclical buffer at 2%, and warned that higher borrowing costs, Middle East energy prices and AI-related lending raise the chance of several risks arriving together. It said the rise in UK gilt yields since July mainly reflects higher expected Bank Rate, driven by energy prices and resilient growth, which is consistent with the pound's support from a possible December rise; the report itself left the pound little changed.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped briefly as London trading got going
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3112 at 11:44 Dubai to about 1.3096 by 11:53, then recovered to about 1.3105 by 12:05 and was near 1.3103 at 12:39. EUR/USD fell by about half as much over the same minutes, from about 1.0974 to about 1.0967, so the dip was partly a firmer dollar and partly the pound's own, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound while it lasted. No report read names a cause, and trading is thin with US markets shut for Thanksgiving; the standing picture is unchanged, with markets putting almost 80% odds on a Bank of England rise on 17 December.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as European trading begins
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3099 at 11:10 Dubai to about 1.3112 by 11:32, its highest since Wednesday evening, and was near 1.3111 at 11:38. EUR/USD rose by a similar share over the same half hour, from about 1.0964 to about 1.0972, so this was the dollar softening as European desks opened rather than UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a cause, and trading is expected to stay thin with US markets shut for Thanksgiving.

feed.title: Sterling has drifted lower in thin holiday trade overnight
feed.text: GBP/USD touched about 1.3127 late on Wednesday evening, then eased through the night from about 1.3112 at 21:41 Dubai to about 1.3096 by 07:38 Dubai on Thursday. EUR/USD slipped by a similar share over the same hours, from about 1.0973 to about 1.0959, so this was a slight firming of the dollar rather than UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a cause; Reuters described the dollar as steady in Asia after a one week low, with trading thin because US markets are shut for Thanksgiving.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened across the board this evening
feed.text: GBP/USD climbed from about 1.3063 at 20:20 Dubai to a high of about 1.3119 at 21:20, including a quick rise from about 1.3085 to 1.3106 between 20:49 and 21:04, and was near 1.3114 at 21:38. EUR/USD rose by a similar share over the same hour, from about 1.0944 to about 1.0981, so this was the dollar weakening rather than UK news, which means more dirhams per pound. No report read names a cause for the evening move itself; US Treasury yields had already fallen about 10 basis points on the day despite the firmer inflation figure, with the two year yield at about 4.58% and the ten year at about 4.82%, and lower US yields tend to weigh on the dollar.

feed.title: Governor Bailey has told MPs further rate rises are likely if energy stays dear
feed.text: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey told the Treasury Committee it is more likely than not that the Bank will have to raise rates again if energy prices stay high, and said the jobs market has stopped softening and flattened out. Signals of further Bank of England rises tend to support the pound, and his remarks were reported as sterling recovered its dip during the hearing.

feed.title: Sterling has recovered its dip during the Bank of England hearing
feed.text: The pound fell a little further after the last update, to a low of about 1.3043 at 18:42 Dubai, while Governor Bailey and other members of the Bank's rate-setting committee were still giving evidence to MPs, then climbed back to about 1.3067 by 19:08 and was near 1.3067 at 19:38. The move was again the pound's own, since EUR/USD drifted slightly lower over the same hour, from about 1.0945 to about 1.0940, so it points to UK news rather than the dollar. No report read yet says what the Bank's policymakers told MPs, so the cause of the dip and the recovery is not known; before the hearing, LSEG data cited by Reuters put about an 80% chance on a further Bank of England rise in December, and dirhams per pound are now back near where they were before the hearing began.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped while the Bank of England faces MPs
feed.text: Governor Bailey and three other members of the Bank's rate-setting committee began giving evidence to the Treasury Committee on the November Monetary Policy Report at 18:15 Dubai, but no report read yet says what they told MPs. A hint that the Bank is in less of a hurry to raise rates again would tend to weigh on the pound, and the move was the pound's own rather than the dollar's: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3068 at 18:23 Dubai to about 1.3052 by 18:38, while EUR/USD held steady near 1.0946, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: US growth and inflation have come in above forecast
feed.text: The second estimate put US growth in the third quarter at an annual rate of 4.3%, well above the 3.5% expected and up from 3.4% in the first estimate, and core PCE inflation for October rose 0.3% on the month as forecast but 3.3% on the year against 3.2% expected. Faster growth and firmer inflation usually support the case for Fed rises, which tends to strengthen the dollar and mean fewer dirhams per pound. In the event the dollar weakened slightly at first: GBP/USD dipped to about 1.3062 at the release, rose to about 1.3076 within a minute, then settled back near 1.3067 by 17:40 Dubai, and none of the sources checked explains the first move up.

feed.title: Sterling has edged back up as the dollar eases before the US figures
feed.text: The dollar gave back part of its morning gain in the hour before the US inflation and growth figures at 17:30 Dubai, falling against the euro as well as the pound, but none of the news sources checked names a cause for the move. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3055 at 16:03 Dubai to a high of about 1.3077 at 16:21, then settled near 1.3068 by 16:38, and EUR/USD rose by a similar share over the same minutes, which means slightly more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped further as the dollar firms ahead of US inflation figures
feed.text: The dollar has held firmer through the European morning, with the dollar index above 104 and up about 0.2% on the day, FXStreet reported, as markets wait for US core PCE inflation at 17:30 Dubai, expected to rise to 3.2% a year from 3.1%. GBP/USD moved between about 1.3066 and 1.3079 from 10:40 to 13:16 Dubai, then fell to about 1.3060 by 13:34, a larger fall than the euro's, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. FXStreet listed a Treasury Committee hearing on the Bank of England's November report with Governor Bailey for today, but no report read explains the drop at 13:20 Dubai, so its cause is not known.

feed.title: The dollar has edged higher as the Asian share sell-off deepens
feed.text: The fall in Asian shares deepened through Wednesday morning, with Taiwan's main index down 7.4%, South Korea's KOSPI down 6% and Japan's Nikkei down 3.3%, Investing.com reported, as worries about planned US tariffs on 16 trading partners and about AI spending hit chip makers; investors bought US government bonds, and markets still see a Fed rise on 9 December as almost certain. Sharp share falls and a firm Fed outlook both tend to draw money into the dollar, and it crept up against the pound and the euro by similar shares, so this was the dollar firming rather than UK news: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3088 at 07:40 Dubai to about 1.3079 at 09:40 and a low of about 1.3073 at 10:15, and was near 1.3076 at 10:30, while EUR/USD slipped from about 1.0943 to about 1.0933, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a single new cause for this morning's drift, and traders are waiting for US inflation and growth figures at 17:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as Asian shares fall on US tariff worries
feed.text: Asian shares fell sharply on Wednesday morning, with the MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan down 2.3% and South Korea and Taiwan down more than 5% at worst, after Reuters reported that the US Trade Representative is preparing findings of a probe into excess capacity among 16 trading partners, and after the Nasdaq fell 1.5% overnight. Sharp falls in shares tend to send investors towards the dollar, and it edged up against both the pound and the euro: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3111 at the last update to about 1.3107 at 04:00 Dubai, then to about 1.3094 by 07:00 and was near 1.3092 at 07:38, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, so dirhams per pound are slightly lower. Brent oil opened 0.5% lower at $90.97 a barrel (about £69.50) after settling more than 2% higher on Tuesday on reports of fresh attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz.

feed.title: Sterling has held its gains as US yields slip on the tariff reports
feed.text: Weaker US shares after the reports of new US tariffs pushed investors into government bonds, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 4.88%, its lowest since 10 November, FXStreet reported, which leaves the dollar index near 103.77 against Monday's 20-month high of 104.53. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold, but markets still price a quarter point Fed rise on 9 December, so the dollar has eased only a little rather than fallen. GBP/USD dipped to a low of about 1.3096 at 19:42 Dubai, rose to a high of about 1.3121 at 21:57 and was near 1.3111 at 23:39, a little above about 1.3105 at the last update, so dirhams per pound are slightly higher.

feed.title: US consumer confidence has jumped well above forecasts
feed.text: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose to 103.3 in November, its highest since January 2025, against about 92.4 expected and 91.9 in October, with the Conference Board pointing to less uncertainty after the midterm elections and lower petrol prices. A stronger US consumer supports the case for further Fed rises and so tends to firm the dollar, but the reaction was small: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3110 at 19:00 Dubai to a low of about 1.3100 by 19:15, then recovered to about 1.3110 by 19:27 and was near 1.3106 at 19:38, so dirhams per pound are little changed. FXStreet reported that the dollar index stayed below 104.00, as the losses that followed the tariff reports earlier this evening outweighed the strong figure.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened after reports of new US tariffs
feed.text: The Wall Street Journal reported at about 17:38 Dubai that the US is preparing higher tariffs on China, the European Union and 14 other trading partners, and US share futures fell sharply, with Nasdaq futures down about 2.4%, FXStreet reported. The dollar's recent strength has leaned on a rally in US technology shares, and it gave ground across the board as they fell: GBP/USD rose steadily from about 1.3089 at 17:34 Dubai to about 1.3108 by 18:39, and EUR/USD by a slightly larger share, which means more dirhams per pound. Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said earlier that falls in inflation have stalled and argued for another rise, and a weekly ADP reading showed slower US private hiring, but neither moved the rate at the time.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped as the euro firms on talk of an ECB rise
feed.text: ECB policymaker Gediminas Simkus said on Tuesday that the central bank should act sooner rather than later and called the weak euro another inflationary factor, after German business confidence rose for a seventh month to 90.6 against 90.5 expected, FXStreet reported. The euro is the largest weight in the dollar index, so a firmer euro pulled the dollar back across the board: EUR/USD rose from about 1.0930 at 14:40 Dubai to about 1.0955, and GBP/USD climbed steadily from about 1.3064 to about 1.3087 by 16:38, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a US cause, and the dollar remains near its strongest since April 2025 ahead of US consumer confidence at 19:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased a little across the board, with no clear cause
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3047 at 13:00 Dubai to a high of about 1.3070 at 14:10 and was near 1.3061 at 14:35, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0915 to about 1.0931, so this was the dollar giving back a little ground rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. German business confidence improved in November, investingLive reported, which may have helped the euro, but no report read names a US or UK cause, and the dollar remains close to its strongest since early 2025 ahead of US consumer confidence this evening.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up in quiet London trade as the dollar holds firm
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped to a low of about 1.3027 at 11:00 Dubai as London opened, then rose from about 1.3033 at 12:29 to about 1.3049 by 12:36 with no news that explains the move, and was near 1.3048 at 12:38, a little above about 1.3038 at the last update. The dollar is holding near its strongest since April 2025 despite the rebound in shares, with analysts pointing to Treasury yields and Fed rise bets, while Brent oil near $89 a barrel (about £68) sits close to a three-month low even after Iran said three tankers hit mines, which takes some support away from the dollar.
